full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 29-9-2019 passed by the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka in Family Appeal No. 83 of 2018 dismissing the appeal and affirming the order dated 11-3-2018 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, and Family Court, Dhaka in Family Execution Case No. 186. of 2014 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the order dated 11-3-2018 passed in Family Execution Case No. 186 of 2014 was stayed for a period of 6 months and after the expiry of the period of stay, no further step for extension of the same was taken. 

 3. Facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the opposite party-plaintiff married' the petitioner on 6-8-2010, fixing the dower money at Taka 80,000 only. After two and half years of the marriage, the petitioner drove out his wife from his house on 13-5-2013. Hence, the plaintiff-opposite party instituted Family Suit No. 124 of 2014 praying for a decree to pay her dower money of Taka 80,000 along with monthly maintenance for nine months @ Taka 2,000 per month. The suit was decreed ex part by judgment and decree dated 20-7-2014. The plaintiff-opposite party then filed Family Execution Case No. 186 of 2014. The defendant-judgment-debtor-petitioner neither appeared in the Court nor paid the decretal amount to the plaintiff-opposite party. The execution Court issued a warrant of arrest and accordingly, Police arrested and produced the petitioner before the Court. The execution Court enlarged the petitioner on bail subject to payment of Taka 30,000 within 7 days from 27-2-2017. The petitioner deposited Taka 5,000 on 6-3-2017, Taka 30.000 on 12-3-2017 and Taka 5,000 on 26-4-17, which in total figure stands at Taka 40,000. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the order dated 11-3-218, the petitioner as appellant filed Family Appeal No. 83 of 2018 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The appeal was transferred to the Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka and upon hearing the parties, the Court dismissed the appeal on 29-9-2019 and affirmed the order dated 11-3-2018 passed in Family Execution Case No. 186 of 1014. 

 10. In support of his contention, he refers to the case of Maksuda Akhter vs Md Serajul Islam, reported in 51 DLR 554.
